هَامِدٌ and ↓ هَمِدٌ and ↓ هَمِيدٌ (tropical:) In a state of death, or extinction]. (M, L.) ―
-b2- هَامِدٌ (tropical:) A garment, or piece of cloth, [dissundered and] wornout by being long folded, so as, when touched, to fall to pieces: (A:) or anything old and wornout: (L, Msb:) pl. هُمَّدٌ. (A.) See 1. ―
-b3- أَرْضٌ هَامِدَةٌ (tropical:) Land in which is no herbage: (S:) and in the same sense هَامِدٌ is applied to a place: (K:) or sterile land, (A, L,) the herbage of which is dried up and broken, (A,) or containing no herbage except what is dried up and broken: (L:) dry and dusty: pl. هَوَامِدُ. (L.) ―
-b4- هَامِدٌ (tropical:) Old and worn-out or wasted, blackened, and changed, [for the worse]. (K.) ―
-b5- (tropical:) A tree black and wasted: (L:) or dried up; (A;) as also herbage. (S, L, K.) ―
-b6- (tropical:) Fruit black and stinking. (A, L.) ―
-b7- (tropical:) A date just ripe, thickskinned and yellow. (TA.) رَمَادٌ هَامِدٌ Ashes [in a state of extinction or] wasted, (L,) and compacted together, and changed in appearance. (A, L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
